title: Meiosis
examples: What is the main difference between meiosis and mitosis?
How does meiosis help create genetic diversity?
Can you explain what crossing over actually involves?

explain.say: Meiosis is a special type of cell division process. It is how we make sex cells like sperm and eggs. This process is very important for life to continue.
The first main goal of meiosis is halving the number of chromosomes. A normal body cell has a full set, but sex cells need half that amount. This keeps the species count steady.
Another key result of meiosis is introducing genetic variation. This means the resulting cells are not exact copies of the parent cell. Variation is what drives evolution forward.
The third important event is crossing over during prophase I. This involves the exchange of segments between homologous chromosomes. It is a major source of new combinations.
In everyday life, meiosis is happening when you are making reproductive cells. For example, when a person makes sperm, meiosis ensures the sperm carries only half the necessary chromosomes.
A common mistake is thinking meiosis is just like mitosis. Remember that mitosis makes identical body cells, but meiosis specifically reduces the chromosome number.

faq.q: Why do we need meiosis if mitosis also divides cells?
faq.a: Mitosis makes body cells for growth and repair, keeping the chromosome number the same. Meiosis is needed to create sex cells, which must have half the chromosomes.
asks: What is the difference between the two divisions?
Why can't we just use mitosis to make eggs?

faq.q: What exactly is crossing over and why is it important?
faq.a: Crossing over is when parts of two different chromosomes swap genetic material. This mixing creates new combinations of genes, which increases variation.
asks: Does crossing over change the genes?
What is the role of crossing over in evolution?

faq.q: How does meiosis ensure the correct number of chromosomes in the next generation?
faq.a: Meiosis involves two rounds of division, which together reduce the chromosome number from diploid to haploid. This prevents the offspring from having too many or too few chromosomes.
asks: Why is the chromosome count halved?
What is the goal of the two meiotic divisions?

faq.q: Is every cell in the body going through meiosis?
faq.a: No, only cells destined to become sex cells, like sperm or eggs, undergo meiosis. Most body cells divide by mitosis throughout life.
asks: When does meiosis happen in a person's life?

faq.a: Yes, the combination of halving and crossing over ensures that the resulting gametes are genetically unique. This variation is key for species survival.

facts: Meiosis results in four daughter cells from one parent cell.
The chromosome number is halved from diploid (2n) to haploid (n).
Crossing over occurs during Prophase I of meiosis.
The resulting cells are gametes, such as sperm or egg cells.

quiz.say: If a normal body cell has twenty chromosomes, how many will the resulting sex cells have after meiosis?
quiz.why: Meiosis halves the chromosome number from diploid to haploid, so twenty becomes ten.

wrong.0: This is wrong because mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same, not meiosis.
wrong.1: This is wrong because doubling the chromosomes happens in DNA replication, not the division process itself.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the reduction is by half, not by a factor of four.

quiz.say: What process involves the exchange of segments between homologous chromosomes?
quiz.why: Crossing over is the specific term for the physical exchange of genetic material between chromosomes.

wrong.1: Mitosis is cell division, not the exchange of genetic material between pairs.
wrong.2: Halving describes the outcome, but crossing over describes the physical event.
wrong.3: Replication is copying genes, but crossing over is swapping sections between pairs.

quiz.say: If a species has 2n chromosomes, what is the chromosome count of its gametes after meiosis?
quiz.why: The defining feature of meiosis is reducing the chromosome count from the full diploid number (2n) to the haploid number (n).

wrong.0: This suggests the chromosome number is quadrupled, which is not what meiosis does.
wrong.1: This suggests dividing the haploid number by two, which is not the biological process.
wrong.3: This would mean the sex cells are the same as body cells, which is incorrect for reproduction.
